Total Precipitation - The annual mean total precipitation over most of eastern Montana ranges from 12 to 16 inches. Colstrip receives an average of about 15.0 inches of precipitation annually. Approximately 45 percent of this total can be expected to fall during the period May through July. Thundershowers can be expected to occur on an average of about 30 days per year (U.S. Department of Commerce, 1975 b). Such thundershower activity can vary greatly in extent and amount of rainfall and may occasionally be accompanied by hail and strong winds. May and June have the two highest monthly precipitation averages with 2.22 and 2.33 inches, respectively. December, January and February have the least with less than 0.6 inches each. Available records indicate that annual rainfall in the region may vary from the mean by as much as seven inches.
On-site total precipitation data were collected from April 16, 1975, through November 30, 1975, at Sarpy Creek. The total for the 7 1/2 months of record was 12.21 inches.
The National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has calculated the estimated return periods for various precipitation events. Representative data for the Sarpy Creek area are presented in Table II-1.
Snowfall - An annual average of about 45.8 inches of snow was recorded at Colstrip during a 26-29 year period prior to and including 1960.
